ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The graph plots percent saturation of hemoglobin on the y-axis against pO2 in mm Hg on the x-axis. There are two oxygen dissociation curves: the fetal hemoglobin curve is labeled near the upper/left curve, and the maternal hemoglobin curve is labeled near the lower/right curve. At a common saturation level such as about 80% or 90%, the fetal curve reaches that saturation at a lower pO2 than the maternal curve. Reasoning: If a hemoglobin curve reaches the same percent saturation at a lower pO2, that hemoglobin has a higher affinity for oxygen. Since fetal hemoglobin requires a lower pO2 than maternal hemoglobin for the same saturation, fetal hemoglobin has greater oxygen affinity.
